name: smartEngin MeetMix
author: smartEngin

sections.description:
smartEngin MeetMix lets visitors book appointments directly on your website. You define your appointment types and weekly hours; visitors pick a free slot and receive a confirmation with a calendar file and a link to cancel or reschedule — no customer account needed.

What you get

  • Appointment types — phone call, online meeting, you visit the customer, the customer visits you. Each with its own duration, buffer times, lead time and booking horizon, and optionally its own weekly hours.
  • A booking page you place with a shortcode. Visitors see your real availability in their own time zone.
  • Double bookings are prevented by the database, not by a lucky guess. Two visitors can click the same slot at the same moment; only one gets it.
  • Emails that arrive — confirmation with a calendar file, notification to you, reminders before the appointment. Every template can be edited, and reminders run without a paid service.
  • Your own form fields next to the seven standard ones — text, several lines, email, phone, address, a choice list, a tick box or a date of birth (entered with the date picker of the browser). Per appointment type you decide what is required, optional or hidden.
  • Your customer can cancel or reschedule through a link that contains nothing but a random value. No account, no password.
  • Your own calendar in the admin area — year, month, week and day. Create an appointment by clicking into it, drag it to a new time, cancel it — and you always see the email to your customer before it goes out.
  • Absences with their own colour, an optional yearly repeat, and a switch for whether they block bookings at all — a birthday should not close your working day.
  • Public holidays for all sixteen German federal states, each one individually selectable.
  • Privacy built in: no IP address is ever stored, old bookings are anonymised or deleted on a schedule you set, and the customer link never carries a name or an email address.
  • Works with multilingual sites. The language a visitor booked in is stored with the booking, and every email to that person switches to it — no forced site language, so WPML, Polylang and TranslatePress keep working.
  • The colours follow yours. One accent colour, used everywhere.
  • A manual inside the admin area, and a log that tells you whether an email really went out.

The Pro extension

smartEngin MeetMix Pro is a separate plugin. It adds Google Calendar in both directions with an own Google Meet room per appointment, Telegram messages to your phone, several booking pages, events with a waiting list, paid appointments through the free smartEngin buy plugin, a minimum age per appointment type, and your calendar on your phone. Nothing in this plugin is locked or waiting to be unlocked — the free plugin is complete in itself, and the extension brings its own code.

What it adds, in one line each: Google Calendar in both directions · an own Google Meet room per appointment · Telegram messages to your phone · several booking views · events with seat limits and a waiting list · paid appointments through the free smartEngin buy plugin · a minimum age per appointment type · your calendar on your phone. Details: smartengin.de/meetmix

External services

This plugin contacts no external server at all. Nothing is loaded from a CDN, no data leaves the visitor’s browser to a third party, and no IP address is stored — the spam protection turns it into a one-way value that expires after an hour. The Pro extension is where Google and Telegram come in, and it asks for those credentials itself.

Bundled library

FullCalendar 6.1.19 (fullcalendar.io, MIT licence) is shipped inside the plugin so that no visitor request ever goes to a CDN. The readable source of the shipped files is at github.com/fullcalendar/fullcalendar; the exact files, versions and download addresses are documented in assets/vendor/fullcalendar/LIESMICH.txt inside the plugin.
sections.installation:
1. Install the plugin and activate it.
  2. Open smartEngin MeetMix → Appointment types and create your first type — a phone call, a visit, an online meeting. Duration, buffer times and how far ahead it can be booked belong to the type.
  3. Open Availability and set your bookable hours per weekday. Absences and German public holidays are on the same page.
  4. Put the shortcode [smartengin_termin] on any page — that is your booking page. [smartengin_booking] does the same thing under an English name.
  5. Check Settings → General for your company name and the address that notifications are sent to.

One thing worth checking once: under Settings → General of WordPress itself, your time zone should be a city (for example Berlin), not a fixed offset such as UTC+2. A fixed offset knows no daylight saving time, and every appointment would shift by an hour in autumn. The plugin warns you about this in red if it finds it.
sections.faq:
Does the visitor need an account?

No. Booking asks only for the fields you chose. The link to cancel or reschedule contains a long random value and nothing else — no name, no email address, no booking number.

What happens if two visitors click the same slot at the same second?

One gets it, the other is told the slot has just been taken. This is decided by the database through a unique key per time unit, not by a check in PHP that could be a moment too late.

Do the reminders work without a paid service?

Yes. They run on WordPress’ own scheduled tasks, and they catch up on whatever is due instead of demanding an exact moment — so a quiet site does not silently skip them. Every reminder is sent once, recorded in the database. WordPress’ scheduler only runs when somebody visits your site; if your site is quiet for long stretches, set up a real cron job at your host. The plugin shows you under Settings → Reminders whether the scheduler is healthy, and how to set that up.

Is any personal data sent anywhere?

No. The plugin contacts no external server. No IP address is stored — the spam protection turns it into a one-way value that cannot be turned back and expires after an hour. Under Settings → Privacy you set how long booking data is kept and whether old bookings are anonymised or deleted.

Does it work on a multilingual site?

Yes, and it deliberately does not force a language. The language a visitor booked in is stored with the booking, and every email to that person switches to it — including the reminder that goes out from a scheduled task. WPML, Polylang and TranslatePress keep working, because nothing here hooks the site locale. Your own wording (email templates, the names of your appointment types) is never machine-translated.

Can I charge for an appointment?

Not with this plugin alone. Paid appointments need the Pro extension together with the free smartEngin buy plugin, which handles checkout, invoice, coupons and refunds. There is deliberately no second payment system in here. You can enter a price without them, but nothing is ever charged, and the plugin says so on the appointment type.

Which third-party code ships with the plugin?

One library: FullCalendar 6.1.19 (MIT). It is shipped inside the plugin instead of loaded from a CDN, so that no visitor request ever leaves your site. Its readable source is at github.com/fullcalendar/fullcalendar, and assets/vendor/fullcalendar/LIESMICH.txt in the plugin names the exact files and where they came from.

What happens to my data if I delete the plugin?

Nothing, unless you ask for it. Deleting the plugin keeps your appointments and settings, so an accidental click never costs you your bookings. There is a switch under Settings → Privacy if you really want everything removed.
sections.changelog:
1.2.4

  • AI connection: every setting of an event is now readable for an AI that helps you set things up (persons per registration, names of companions, e-mail confirmation, payment deadline for people moving up, end of the waiting list, free seats shown, colour, design). Texts that are not meant for the public – the description, the address and the access link – appear only as “set” or “not set”. With MeetMix Pro the appearance of each event and the shared button settings are added.

1.2.3

  • The MeetMix logo under the calendar is loaded with the plugin version in its address, like stylesheets and scripts. After an update every browser now shows the current logo instead of an old saved copy.

1.2.2

  • The MeetMix logo under the calendar (only shown when you switch it on under Settings → Design): “Engin” in “smartEngin” is now brown (#6B4A33) instead of green.

1.2.1

  • Settings → Design: an add-on can offer ready-made accent colours as extra buttons next to “Back to the standard colour” (filter seca_akzent_vorlagen). MeetMix Pro uses it for “Alpenglow colours”.

1.2.0

  • Events: one sign-up can now bring several people (database schema 20). Seats count people, not sign-ups: a sign-up with 3 people takes 3 seats. Existing sign-ups count as 1 person, so all numbers stay the same.
  • Free events always take exactly 1 person per sign-up, as protection against spam. This rule sits in the database function itself, not only in the form.
  • Waiting list with groups: whoever fits first moves up. A group keeps its place at the front and comes in as soon as there are enough free seats for all of them; a group is never split.
  • For developers: SECA_Store::event_max_personen() and the filter seca_event_max_personen, SECA_Store::event_anmeldung_personen_setzen(), SECA_Store::event_anmeldungen_zahl(), new return values -4 and -5 of event_anmeldung_anlegen().

1.1.0

  • Settings, Overview: new table “Which appointment type can be booked where?”. For every appointment type and booking view it says whether visitors can book it, and if not, why and what to do: switched off, not ticked in the booking view, payment without a payment route, minimum age without a check. It also warns when nobody can book although the type is offered (no weekly hours, no free time in the coming weeks), shows the next free time and notes a booking view that is not on any published page.
  • Appointment types: the list shows “Bookable” or “Not bookable” with the reason for every type. A new appointment type is now bookable by default.
  • For developers: new filters seca_buchbarkeit_hinweise, seca_mail_html and seca_mails_vor_testmail (the finished customer email, with its building blocks). The standard email layout is unchanged.

1.0.2

  • Calendar: when you add an absence, the “To” date now follows the “From” date. For a single day you only pick one date. If you chose a later “To” date on purpose (several days), it stays; it never ends up before the “From” date, so saving no longer fails because of a forgotten “To” date. Works in the backend calendar and in the phone calendar.

1.0.1

  • Calendar: the appointment window has a new button “Move appointment”. Pick a new date and time, then you see the email to your customer before anything is sent, as with dragging. It works for any week and on phones and tablets, where dragging is hard.

1.0.0

  • The optional smartEngin MeetMix logo under the booking calendar now links to the MeetMix page on smartengin.de (new tab). It is still off by default, and the switch says so. If you switched the logo on in an earlier version, it stays without a link until you save that setting again. With your own logo (Pro) there is no link.

0.45.10

  • German (and every other language the plugin ships) is now complete right after an update. When WordPress also has a language pack from translate.wordpress.org, it used to read only that pack, and texts added since its last update stayed in English. The translation inside the plugin is now loaded first and the pack stays behind it as a fallback.

0.45.9

  • New switch per booking view under “Picture above the appointment type”: “AI label”. When it is on, layouts with a picture (Pro: “Card and steps”) show a small “AI-generated” note in the bottom right corner of the picture. Off by default.

0.45.8

  • The booking calendar no longer jumps while the page loads. It stays invisible for the split second until the days are drawn and the columns are arranged for the screen width, then appears complete. If the script cannot run, it still appears after three seconds.
  • The short “Loading …” note in the time column is now exactly as tall as the “Please pick a day.” note that replaces it, so the time zone field below it stays in place.

upgrade_notice.1.2.0: Events can take several people in one sign-up (needed by MeetMix Pro 1.6.0). Free events stay at one person per sign-up. Existing sign-ups and all numbers stay as they are.
upgrade_notice.1.1.0: New overview of which appointment type can be booked where, and why not. New appointment types are bookable by default. Your emails look exactly as before.
upgrade_notice.1.0.0: Version 1.0.0: German is complete right after every update, the booking calendar no longer jumps while it loads, and the optional MeetMix logo (off by default) links to smartengin.de.
upgrade_notice.0.43.0: Reports blocked attempts to smartEngin Analytics, if it is installed. Without Analytics nothing changes.
upgrade_notice.0.42.4: Adds the date-of-birth field type, a note about the minimum age in Pro, and stops browser autofill from tripping the spam trap.
upgrade_notice.0.42.3: Stops browser autofill from tripping the spam trap on the booking form.
upgrade_notice.0.42.2: Fixes real visitors being turned away as “automated” when their browser auto-filled the booking form.
upgrade_notice.0.42.1: The minimum age of an appointment type can now be any number of years (set with MeetMix Pro 0.56.1). The manual explains the “Date of birth” field type.
upgrade_notice.0.42.0: Adds the form field type “Date of birth”. Nothing changes on your booking page until you create such a field.
upgrade_notice.0.41.0: Fixes bookings with very long names, adds a brake against programs that flood the booking calendar with requests, and prepares confirmation by email for event sign-ups.
upgrade_notice.0.40.0: A clear window instead of a small line when the time you pick for an appointment is taken — and a warning for absences, events and holidays.
upgrade_notice.0.39.0: New overview of blocked attacks under Settings → Log. Only numbers are stored, no IP addresses. Your spam protection itself works exactly as before.
upgrade_notice.0.38.0: You can now drag the appointment types of a booking view into the order your visitors see, and give a single appointment type its own booking confirmation with attachments. Nothing changes until you do it.
upgrade_notice.0.33.3: Screenshot descriptions for the plugin directory. Nothing about the plugin itself has changed.
upgrade_notice.0.33.2: The admin calendar now fills the height of your window instead of a fixed height. Nothing you click changes.
upgrade_notice.0.33.1: The reschedule calendar on the customer page loads its script the way the plugin directory asks for. Nothing you can see changes.
upgrade_notice.0.33.0: Every page is now filtered once more at the moment it is printed, as the plugin directory asks. Nothing you can see changes.
upgrade_notice.0.32.3: An internal page used for building the plugin has been removed. Nothing you can see or click changes.
upgrade_notice.0.32.2: Documentation only. Nothing about how the plugin works has changed.
upgrade_notice.0.32.1: A slot is now held for 30 minutes while somebody pays, instead of 15 - long enough for payment methods that send your customer to a site of their own.

screenshots.caption: The booking page a visitor sees: your appointment types, your real free times, and the times in the visitor's own time zone.
Your calendar in the admin area, month view — with the window for a new appointment or an absence open.
The week view: every appointment in its real length and in the colour of its type.
The year view: one glance shows which days are busy and where your absences are.
Settings: the name and address your emails go out under, the booking number, and what your customer is allowed to change.
Availability: your bookable hours per weekday. Absences and German public holidays live on the same page.
Your appointment types with duration, kind and status — drag a row to change the order your visitors see.
The manual inside the admin area: every part of the plugin explained where you need it.
